hook: "Here's every element of my highest-ROAS YouTube ad format ever broken down into one tweet. (Save this one…)"
body: The full anatomy: Hook (0-3s) = bold visual pattern break + outcome text overlay ('I cleared my acne in 14 days,' not 'introducing our serum'). Format = claymation 9-shot, 30s: problem → villain (mechanism as clay monster) → villain escalation → hero ingredient defeats villain → mechanism at work → product reveal → transformation → social proof → CTA. The villain is the converter — the product is the WEAPON. CTA in the last 3s only: one offer, one action, text overlay on hero shot. Offer must break the category pattern (not another 20% off). Guarantee as text overlay. Targeting: custom intent. Placement: 6s unskippable Shorts bumper from the winning 30s.
idea: The highest-ROAS YouTube format: outcome-text hook + 9-shot claymation villain arc (problem → villain → hero ingredient → product → transformation → proof → CTA) with the CTA only in the last 3 seconds.
sequencing: The hook: 0-3s pattern break + outcome text overlay.
The format: claymation 9-shot — handmade signal vs AI slop.
The pacing: 9 shots x 2-4s.
The arc: problem, villain, escalation, hero wins, mechanism, reveal, transformation, proof, CTA.
The insight: the villain converts; the product is the weapon.
The CTA: last 3s only — one offer, one action, text overlay.
Offer + guarantee: break the category pattern; risk reversal as overlay.
Targeting + placement: custom intent; 6s Shorts bumper cutdown. CTA: DM YT.
formatting: Mega-breakdown tweet: hook/format/pacing/CTA/offer/guarantee/targeting/placement sections. 'Save this one' framing. Animated GIF.
why_it_works: The villain gives the viewer an enemy to root against — narrative transportation past the skip button. 'Product as weapon' makes the pitch feel like a story climax, not an interruption.
what_to_steal: The 9-shot villain arc is LC's premium video skeleton: problem (green skin) → villain (cheap-plating monster) → hero (PVD waterproof) → mechanism → reveal → transformation → proof → CTA. 'CTA in the last 3s only — every second before earns the right to ask' is LC's pacing rule.

hook: "Out top 4 YouTube ad formats printing the hardest right now, mapped to awareness stage and market sophistication: (Prompts included. Bookmark this)"
body: Four formats mapped to awareness: (1) Unaware/low sophistication: claymation 9-shot villain arc, 30s — with a copy-paste prompt included. (2) Problem-aware/medium: hybrid AI UGC, 30s talking to camera — AI for production, real humans for trust elements; fix robotic voice/movement with real VO, accents, ElevenLabs. (3) Solution-aware/high: 15s cinematic product film, no dialogue — 4 shots: macro texture, hero reveal in dramatic lighting, lifestyle context, CTA card; 'creative quality alone can become your USP.' (4) Remarketing: unskippable 6s Shorts bumper. Includes transcripts of example ads (Hume Pod, Manjaro scan, Shanghai vlog).
